I am not on any of the utility bills, lease, or mortgage. My son has not been in the Texas Juvenile Justice system either. How can I provide proof of residency? How do I create a Parent Portal account?

Parents please click here to create your Parent Portal Account (opens in new tab)

Parents, if you have not created your account, please visit our Parent Portal Registration (opens in new tab) page. The Parent portal will allow you to monitor your child's progress in school by providing timely access to both assignments and grades that are entered by the teacher throughout the grading period. You will also have the ability to contact your student's teacher via the "Communications" module inside of Focus.

In order to create a Parent Portal account online, you must have a valid email address. Please note that the email should not be the same as the student's email.

Texas Tech K-12 requires every user to have a unique email address to ensure any communication goes to the intended recipient. Parents and Students cannot share email addresses. The Password Reset Email will not work if more than one user shares an email address. Most ISP or email providers have options for families who need multiple email addresses on the same account for each user.

Prior to starting the account creation process, we ask that if your student has an existing account, you please have their matriculation number and date of birth. The system will request this information to connect the accounts.

For those that do not have an existing account, please click on "I do not have an Account Registered on the Parent Portal but would like to Create One" (opens in new tab).

First Time Access (Creating An Account)

Students, if you have not created your account, please visit our Student Registration (opens in new tab) page. The student portal will allow you to access your courses, monitor your course progress in school by providing timely access to both assignments and grades that are entered by your teacher throughout the grading period. You will also have the ability to contact your teacher via the "Communications" module inside of Focus.

In order to create your account, you must have a valid email address. Please note that the email address should not be the same as another student's email or your parent's email.

Texas Tech K-12 offers several different programs (each program is listed below). Based upon your selection, application requirements may be different:

Step 1: Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) - If you will remain enrolled at your local school, you must obtain prior approval from your school counselor before enrolling in any course or CBE. Failure to obtain approval may result in un-awarded credit for a course or CBE. With prior approval, students enrolled in another school may enroll in:

Step 2: Supplemental courses (opens in new tab)

Step 3: Credit-by-Examinations or CBE's (opens in new tab).

Step 4: Full-Time Texas Tech K-12 Student - If you are withdrawing from your local school district and wish to become a Full-Time Student at Texas Tech K-12, you may apply to:

Step 5: The "Tuition-Free Full-Time Program (opens in new tab)" (Texas Residents), or

Step 6: The "Tuition-Paid Full-Time Program (opens in new tab)" (Outside of Texas or Texas Residents seeking more flexibility).

Step 7: College Preparatory Academy (opens in new tab) - Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time students may earn both high school and college credit simultaneously. These courses are typically offered through partnerships between high schools and colleges or universities, enabling students to get a head start on their college education while still in high school.

Enrollment Requirements

You will need to submit the following documents for your application to be processed:

answer.text:
To provide proof of residency for Texas Tech K-12 enrollment, especially if you are not listed on utility bills, lease, or mortgage, you can consider the following options:

**Proof of Residency Options:**

- **Affidavit of Residency**: You may be able to fill out an affidavit of residency. This document typically requires a statement from the person with whom you are living (such as your parents) affirming that you and your child reside at their address. It may need to be notarized.

- **Additional Supporting Documents**: You might also provide other documents that can help establish residency, such as:
  - A letter from a government agency or employer that includes your address.
  - Medical or insurance documents with your address.
  - Any other official correspondence that includes your address.

For specific guidance and to confirm what documents are acceptable, it is best to contact Texas Tech K-12 directly. They can provide the most accurate and detailed information regarding their residency requirements and any affidavits they may accept.

**Contact Information**:
- Phone: 1-800-692-6877
- Email: ttuk12@ttu.edu

Feel free to reach out to them for further assistance on this matter.
